23.0.0.en: Because of Sarah's great obedience and her trust in God in accompanying Abraham on the journey of faith from his departure from Ur of the Chaldees, the inspired text took care to mention her age, unlike the rest of the women in the Holy Bible: she lived 127 years, and she had borne Isaac at the age of ninety. For this reason the Fathers expect that Isaac's age when he was offered as a sacrifice had exceeded twenty-five or thirty, since his age at the death of his mother was 37 years.

23.1.0.en: Sarah died in the town of Arba, which was later called Hebron. It is in the south of the land of Canaan, near Beersheba. It seems that Abraham had gone out from Hebron to look after some of his work and his shepherds, and when he returned he found that Sarah had died. He grieved over her greatly, and wept and mourned for her, that is, he remembered all her virtues, her love, her companionship with him on the way of faith, and her bearing of many hardships. This is the first time it is mentioned that Abraham wept, because Sarah was the companion of his life, and this shows his love and esteem for her.

23.1.1.en: Care for the faithfulness and sincerity of those around you, praise them for it, and enjoy their love as long as they live with you, because they are an image of God's love offered to you, so let us thank Him for His gifts.

23.2.0.en: The sons of Heth: the sons of Heth were descendants of the son of Canaan; they became a great people called the Hittites and lived in the south of Canaan.

23.2.1.en: Abraham went to one of the cities of the Hittites that was near Hebron and entered their city. At the gate of the city there is a square, as is the custom of cities, where the leaders and judges of the city gather. So he went in to ask them for a place in which to bury Sarah, since he had not owned any place throughout his life, but moved about with his tent in the wilderness, he and his flocks.

23.3.0.en: Abraham declared to the sons of Heth that he was a stranger dwelling among them, despite his greatness and the abundance of his possessions. But he was humble and felt himself a stranger to the world because his heart was attached to heaven. And he asked them for a place in which to bury Sarah.

23.4.0.en: The sons of Heth showed their love for Abraham and their honor toward him, and said to him that his standing among them was that of a great prince, because they saw his wealth and the blessing of God that was with him. And they gladly agreed that he should bury Sarah in whichever of their tombs he chose.

23.5.0.en: The cave of Machpelah: that is, double, because it consists of two chambers, an inner and an outer.

23.5.1.en: Abraham bowed down in humility before the leaders of the people and those sitting in the square, and asked them that he might buy the cave of Machpelah, which lay at the edge of the field of one of the inhabitants of the city, Ephron the son of Zohar. Here Abraham's adherence to his faith appears: he did not bury Sarah in the land of his fathers in Iraq, because they were far from the worship of God, nor in one of the tombs of the Canaanites, the sons of Heth, because they were idolaters, but asked to buy a private burial place for his wife.

23.6.0.en: Ephron, the owner of the land and the cave, was sitting among those sitting in the square. He rose in the midst of those gathered and declared that he was offering his field and the cave in it as a gift to Abraham, with those sitting there as witnesses to it. This shows Ephron's generosity, Abraham's standing among the Hittites, and their effort to honor him.

23.7.0.en: Abraham confirmed his respect and humility by bowing down a second time before the Hittites, and asked Ephron, whom Abraham had not known personally before, to let him buy the field and the cave and not have it be a gift from him. For Abraham had lived as a stranger all his life and had owned nothing except a tomb, that is, death, and he believed God's promise of the inheritance of the land of Canaan, which would be fulfilled for his children.

23.8.0.en: Four hundred shekels of silver: a shekel of silver is approximately 15 grams, and therefore four hundred shekels equal six kilograms of silver.

23.8.1.en: When Ephron saw Abraham's insistence on paying the price of the land, he accepted that he should buy it, declaring that the love between them was more important, and that if he wished to buy it, let it be as he wished.

23.9.0.en: Current money with the merchant: that is, pure silver approved by the merchants and all those dealing in buying and selling.

23.9.1.en: Abraham weighed out the silver, the price of the field, before the elders of the Hittites and gave it to Ephron, and thus Abraham came to own the field, the cave, and the trees that were in the field. So Abraham never owned any land throughout his life, and when he did own some, he owned a burial place, that is, estrangement from the world.

23.9.2.en: May you lift your eyes toward heaven and not be preoccupied with the possessions of the earth, because they pass away. And if you own anything, consider yourself a steward over it, managing it faithfully, so that you will give an account of it on the day of judgment, and use it to show love toward those around you and not for your selfishness and your own pleasures.

23.10.0.en: Finally Abraham buried Sarah in the cave of Machpelah. Afterward Abraham himself was buried in the same cave, along with Isaac and Jacob; the bones of Joseph were also carried to it, and likewise Rebekah and Leah were buried in it. The marriage of Isaac

24.0.s.en: (1) Abraham's sending of the chief of his house

24.0.0.en: Abraham grew old, and his age drew near to 140 years, because Sarah died when he was 137 years old, and after a period of about three years he thought of marrying his son Isaac. God's blessing upon him was great in possessions, in addition to the spiritual blessings.

24.1.0.en: Abraham summoned the chief of his servants, Eliezer of Damascus, who was the manager of his possessions and affairs, and asked him to swear to him by putting his hand under Abraham's thigh ... but why?

24.1.1.en: 1- Swearing by putting the hand under the thigh, near the place of circumcision, is an oath by the covenant of God, and by sonship and belonging to Him.

24.1.2.en: 2- It is an oath by the offspring from whom Christ would come, so it is a great and certain oath.

24.2.0.en: The oath that Abraham asked Eliezer to swear was that he would not choose a wife for his son Isaac from the Canaanite women who lived around him, but that Eliezer should go to Abraham's family living in Mesopotamia and choose a wife from there, because the Canaanite women were wicked and immersed in the worship of idols, while Abraham's clan, though they too were idolaters, were better than they in the knowledge of God.

24.2.1.en: And he did not send Isaac to choose a wife for himself, for the following reasons:

24.2.2.en: 1- Lest his heart become attached and the wife influence him, so that he would settle with her in her land and abandon God's covenant of dwelling in Canaan.

24.2.3.en: 2- It was the custom of the rich at that time to send their servants to choose wives for their sons.

24.3.0.en: Eliezer asked Abraham whether, if he found a suitable girl as a wife and she refused to come to Canaan, he should take Isaac to her and settle with her in her land.

24.4.0.en: Abraham answered his servant as follows:

24.4.1.en: 1- He warned him against taking Isaac back to the land of his clan, but that he should remain in Canaan in obedience to God's commands.

24.4.2.en: 2- He reassured him that God, whom he worshiped, would send His angel before him, choose the wife, and make the matter easy so that she would come with him to Canaan.

24.4.3.en: 3- If no suitable girl was willing to come with him, he would be free from this oath.

24.4.4.en: So Eliezer, the chief of his house, swore to him, by putting his hand under his thigh, that he would go and choose a wife for Isaac from his clan and his family.

24.4.5.en: Be assured that God will help you to carry out His commandments, and do not worry about the surrounding circumstances and the opinion of people, for God persuades them and gives you grace in their eyes, so that you may remain firm in your faith and in your life with them.

24.5.s.en: (2) The sign of the chosen wife

24.5.0.en: Aram-naharaim: a region lying in the north between the Tigris and the Euphrates rivers.

24.5.1.en: The city of Nahor: it lies near Haran, between the two rivers in the north, named after Nahor the grandfather of Abraham, or Nahor the brother of Abraham, who went there after Abraham left it and went to Canaan.

24.5.2.en: Eliezer took ten camels and loaded them with some of the goods of God, as a gift and dowry from his master for the wife whom he would choose.

24.5.3.en: Eliezer is a symbol of the Holy Spirit, who chooses for believers their wives and orders their lives. The number (10) signifies holding fast to God's ten commandments, and the goods signify the blessings of the Holy Spirit which He grants to His children. And the choice of a wife from the Gentiles for Isaac is a type of the acceptance of the Gentiles into faith in Christ.

24.6.0.en: He made the camels kneel down: he made them couch, that is, kneel and rest.

24.6.1.en: Eliezer arrived at the city of Nahor and stood at a well outside the city. It was evening, the time when the girls go out to fill their jars, when the heat of the sun's rays has abated.

24.6.2.en: The well is a symbol of Baptism, and the evening time signifies God's love that visits us before the day ends.

24.7.0.en: Eliezer, who had entered into the faith and been circumcised by Abraham, prayed. He asked God, interceding by Abraham, the beloved of God and His friend, to make it easy for him to reach the suitable girl. He also asked Him for a sign: that he needed to drink, he and the servants with him, and the camels. He would ask the girls who came out to draw water to give him water to drink, and if one of them agreed, and even offered greater love of her own accord by watering him and his camels and all who were with him, she would be the girl whom God had chosen. Thus the sign was overflowing love, or generosity in giving.

24.7.1.en: Your love for those around you and your care for everyone in need is the sign that shows your Christianity to all people, so care for everyone in need and do not turn away anyone who asks you.

24.8.0.en: Immediately after Eliezer finished his prayer, he found Rebekah, the daughter of Bethuel the son of Nahor, Abraham's brother, coming out to draw water. God had granted her great beauty. When she reached the well she went down to it, since it was in a low place, filled her jar with water, and came up to return to her home.

24.9.0.en: Eliezer ran to her and asked her to give him a little water to drink, and weariness was evident on his face from the toil of the journey.

24.10.0.en: Rebekah responded quickly, lowered her jar from her shoulder, put it on her arm, and tilted it so that he might drink from it.

24.11.0.en: After Eliezer had drunk, Rebekah offered love of her own accord, without his asking her, namely to water his camels also, which she saw beside him, and of course she also watered the servants who were with him. This was proof of her generosity and her care for the hospitality of strangers.

24.12.0.en: The trough: a basin in which water is placed for the animals to drink from.

24.12.1.en: Rebekah emptied her jar into the trough, and went to the well and returned several times to fill the trough with water, so that all the camels drank.

24.13.0.en: Eliezer was looking at her intently, seeing the sign he had asked of God being quickly fulfilled before him, and perhaps he kept on praying within himself that God would complete His work.

24.13.1.en: How beautiful it is that you rely on prayer in ordering the affairs of your life! Trust that God rejoices in your prayers and answers quickly according to your faith. Continue in your prayer even if God's answer is delayed for a wisdom He sees, for He gives you at the right time what is for your good.

24.14.0.en: Eliezer was sure that this was the girl whom God had chosen, after the sign was fulfilled, for he had great faith like his master Abraham. So he hastened and put a golden ring in Rebekah's nose and two bracelets of gold on her hands, and asked her who she was and whether there was room and food in their house for him and the camels.

24.15.0.en: The girl told him that she was Rebekah, the daughter of Bethuel the son of Nahor by his wife Milcah, and she welcomed his being hosted, along with his companions and camels.

24.16.0.en: Eliezer rejoiced greatly and bowed down before God and thanked Him, because in the greatness of His love He had guided him not only to one of the clan of his master Abraham, but to the granddaughter of his brother Nahor.

24.17.0.en: Rebekah ran to her home and told her mother and her brothers what had happened to her.

24.18.0.en: When Laban, Rebekah's brother, heard her words about Eliezer and what he had done for her, and saw the ring and the bracelets, he ran to Eliezer, who was still standing by the well, welcomed him, and called him "blessed of the Lord" to honor him, and invited him to enter the house, since he had ordered the servants to prepare a place to host him and those with him.

24.19.0.en: Eliezer entered the house and put his camels in the animals' enclosure, and they gave them water and food, and welcomed him and set a table before him that he might eat. But he said, "I will not eat until I have told my errand," that is, I have declared the mission for which I have come.

24.20.0.en: Eliezer himself made known to Laban and Rebekah's family that he was Abraham's servant, and explained to them the wealth and possessions to which his master had come, in servants, cattle, silver and gold, and that he had one only son, Isaac, who was the heir of all his possessions. And that Abraham had asked him to choose a wife for Isaac from his kindred and clan and bring her to Canaan, and that he had sworn to him to do so, but that if the wife was not willing to come to Canaan, he would be free from his oath.

24.21.0.en: He told them how he had asked God for a sign when he reached the well outside their city, namely that he would ask for water, and the girl who agreed to give him water to drink and then offered to water his camels also would be the girl chosen by God. When he had finished his prayer, Rebekah came, and the sign was fulfilled in her, and when he asked her who she was, she told him that she was Rebekah, the daughter of Bethuel the son of Nahor. So he thanked God, who had guided him to the house of his master's brother, and bowed down to Him, and put the ring and the bracelets on Rebekah's nose and hands as a dowry for her. Then Eliezer asked Rebekah's family whether they agreed to give Rebekah to Isaac or not, so that he might go on his way.

24.21.1.en: It is good that you obey God's word and trust in Him, and even ask a sign from Him to strengthen your faith, for He is a tender God, long-suffering, who cares for you and rejoices in your prayers and makes your way easy so that you may live with Him.

24.22.0.en: Laban and his father Bethuel agreed to give Rebekah in marriage to Isaac, for they understood from the story that God was the one who had chosen her, so they could not oppose Him, and they gave Rebekah to be the wife of Isaac. We note that Laban is mentioned before his father Bethuel, either because of his old age or his illness, so he left his son to lead the situation.

24.22.1.en: Submission to God's will gives your life rest, because you feel that He is the leader and director of your affairs, and He therefore guarantees your rest and your peace. Be careful to understand God's dealings with you, and if you do not understand, lift up your heart with many prayers, and He will reveal and make clear to you His will.

24.23.0.en: Eliezer thanked God for the success of his mission and bowed down to Him, for he was a man of prayer and humility like his master. And he gave gifts to Rebekah and her family, represented by her brother and her mother, as a completion of her dowry, namely vessels of silver and gold, precious things, and garments.

24.24.0.en: Eliezer ate and drank and spent that night in joy, and in the morning he asked leave of Rebekah's family to take her and depart to Abraham.

24.25.0.en: Rebekah's family tried to have her stay with them some days so that they might enjoy her before she left them, and they asked Eliezer for this, that he stay with them for that period.

24.26.0.en: Eliezer begged Rebekah's family not to delay him from departing, since God had declared His will and chosen Rebekah. Her family said, "Let us ask her whether she agrees to depart quickly," and she agreed. We note the girl's freedom in accepting her bridegroom, which is the right of every girl.

24.27.0.en: Thousands of millions: tens of thousands.

24.27.1.en: Possess the gate of those who hate them: overcome his enemies.

24.27.2.en: They bade farewell to their sister and daughter Rebekah and wished for her that God would give her offspring who would be a great nation reaching tens of thousands, and that her offspring would be strong and overcome its enemies. And they gave Rebekah, as was the custom of that time, her nurse, who was called Deborah, and the two went with Eliezer and the servants who were with him to the land of Canaan.

24.28.0.en: Rebekah went out from her house, she and her maidservants whom her family had given her, and they rode on the camels, and the caravan set out, led by Eliezer of Damascus, from Haran to the land of Canaan.

24.29.0.en: Isaac was living in the south of the land of Canaan, and he had gone to look after the shepherds and the cattle at Beer-lahai-roi, where the angel appeared to Hagar and Ishmael (ch. 16:14). At evening, as he was returning to his tent, he went out into the field to spend a time of solitude and meditation on God, as some of the Jews of old were accustomed to do, and many monks do at present. He saw from afar a caravan of camels coming toward the place where he lived.

24.29.1.en: How beautiful it is to set aside a time to be alone with God every day, or at least every week, sitting by yourself in a quiet place, whether a secluded place, or before a wide view, or in a holy place, or before an icon of Christ, and thinking on a spiritual subject and reviewing your life, so that you enjoy a quiet meeting and your feelings go forth toward God.

24.30.0.en: Rebekah noticed a man coming toward them, and out of respect for him she got down from the camel and asked Eliezer of Damascus about him, and he said that he was Isaac. So out of modesty she covered her face with the veil, as was the custom of women at this time.

24.31.0.en: The caravan arrived and met Isaac, and Eliezer told him all that had happened and presented Rebekah to him. Isaac rejoiced in her and brought her into the tent of his mother Sarah, and married her, and was comforted over the departure of his mother by the love that grew with Rebekah and his new life with her. Three years had passed since the death of Sarah, and Isaac had reached forty years of age.

24.31.1.en: The death of Abraham, the birth of Jacob and Esau, and the sale of the birthright
